expected_dmg.formula: 200 to Active (apply Weakness) + 60 to opponent Bench as 6 damage counters (10 each) distributable in any way; counters ignore Weakness/Resistance/effect-immunity; no energy discarded so it repeats every turn once [R,P] is assembled
displayed 0 -> deals 100 to any 1 opponent Pokemon (Bench: no Weakness/Resistance); capped at target remaining HP
move up to 3 damage counters (<=30) from 1 of your Pokemon to 1 opponent Pokemon; requires {D} Energy attached; also heals your own Pokemon by the moved amount
70 flat, cost [C]; fallback when Fire missing

early.until: turn <= 3 and Dragapult ex not yet [R,P]-loaded
early.on_plan: Dreepy in play >=1 (ideally 2), bench built, at least one of Fire/Psychic started on the Dragapult line, Rare Candy or Drakloak secured

mid.until: Dragapult ex has both Fire and Psychic attached
mid.on_plan: first_attack_turn(Phantom Dive #154) <= 4; Phantom Dive every turn; 60 spread concentrated on 1-2 bench threats; Boss's Orders drags softened target

late.on_plan: post_ko_attack_rate >= 0.8; 2nd Dragapult loaded; Cruel Arrow/Munkidori convert spread into extra bench KOs to close 6 prizes

doctrines.name: Rare Candy fast line
doctrines.plan: Dreepy T1 -> Rare Candy T2/T3 straight to Dragapult ex (skip Drakloak); Phantom Dive by T3
doctrines.discriminating_metric: first_attack_turn(154) and play_rate[1079] (Rare Candy) vs play_rate[120] (Drakloak evolve); A/B: Rare-line has lower Drakloak-evolve rate and earlier first_attack_turn

doctrines.name: Manual evolution line
doctrines.plan: Dreepy -> Drakloak (use Recon Directive draw) -> Dragapult ex; save Rare Candy, gain card selection but 1 turn slower
doctrines.discriminating_metric: play_rate[120] Drakloak Recon usage vs first_attack_turn(154); win-rate delta between lines

doctrines.name: Risky Ruins on vs held
doctrines.plan: A: play Risky Ruins aggressively to chip opponent basics and feed Munkidori export; B: keep it in hand and only play when own bench is Dark/high-HP or Munkidori is online
doctrines.discriminating_metric: play_rate[1260] correlated with own-bench damage from RR (self-harm) vs opponent-basic chip; win-rate A vs B

tensions.balance: Fire (only 3 in deck) attaches only to an active Dragapult that already holds or will hold Psychic; never attach Fire to Munkidori/Fezandipiti
keep Risky Ruins only when own bench is Dark/high-HP or Munkidori can export; do not have it out when about to Buddy-Buddy Poffin low-HP basics (Budew 30, Dreepy 70)
stop digging (Ultra Ball / Lillie's) once Phantom Dive is executable THIS turn; never discard/shuffle-away the last Fire energy or the only Dragapult
place the 60 spread on 1-2 Pokemon KO-able within 1-2 turns (their current/next attacker); hold one Boss's Orders to pull the softened target

hypotheses.claim: L0 attaches energy by count/displayed-damage without regard to TYPE, so Dragapult accumulates wrong-type energy (e.g. 2 Psychic, 0 Fire) and Phantom Dive (which strictly requires 1 Fire) is never offered, collapsing the entire win condition to Jet Headbutt (70).
hypotheses.direction: of all attacks Dragapult makes once it has >=2 energy, the fraction that are Phantom Dive (154) rather than Jet Headbutt (153) must be HIGH; energy_attach_share[121] must dominate and include Fire
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: hard 'Fire first' gate can leave Dragapult unable to attack at all on turns when no Fire is drawn (only 3 Fire in the deck) -> non-attacking turns and lost tempo
hypotheses.scenario: Give a Dragapult ex 2 Psychic and 0 Fire (attach only Psychic each turn); confirm Phantom Dive option never appears (verified 504/504) and the deck is stuck on Jet Headbutt; regression: ensure fixed engine routes a Fire before declaring Dragapult 'loaded'
hypotheses.pattern: deck-specific feeding plan (Fire-first to Dragapult) + type-aware loaded check

hypotheses.claim: L0 uses abilities/attacks unconditionally, so Dudunsparce Run Away Draw (shuffles itself into deck) or Meowth ex Tuck Tail (returns itself to hand) can fire when it is the LAST Pokemon in play, emptying the field and losing instantly.
hypotheses.direction: these self-removal effects must NEVER fire when own in-play Pokemon count == 1 (Run Away) or when bench is empty (Tuck Tail)
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: over-gating suppresses a safe 3-card draw / a safe Meowth reset when a bench body exists, costing card advantage
hypotheses.scenario: Reduce own board to just Dudunsparce active with empty bench and a Run Away Draw prompt available (and separately Meowth active, empty bench, 3 energy, Tuck Tail available); confirm the fixed engine refuses both
hypotheses.pattern: board-state gate implementing the §2b declared fire-conditions

hypotheses.claim: Ultra Ball is used unconditionally every turn and discards 2 cards, which can dump the last Fire energy, the only Dragapult, or a Rare Candy, permanently disabling the win condition.
hypotheses.direction: Ultra Ball should not fire when the only legal discards include the last Fire energy / only Dragapult / a needed Rare Candy, and not fire when it advances nothing

threshold.value: Ultra-Ball-that-discards-a-protected-card events <= 0.05 of Ultra Ball plays

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: too strict a protection list starves the search engine and slows finding Dreepy/Dragapult, delaying setup
hypotheses.pattern: possession-based gate (discard-protection list) on unconditional search items

hypotheses.claim: Boss's Orders (gust) target selection ignores the Phantom Dive spread: it pulls a target that is NOT the one already softened to KO range, wasting the 60 spread investment.
hypotheses.direction: gust target should preferentially be a benched Pokemon already damaged (by spread/Munkidori/Cruel Arrow) that becomes KO-able this turn, or the highest-prize KO-able body

threshold.value: share of Boss's Orders whose target is KO'd or left <=0 HP that turn >= 0.6

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: forcing 'only gust a KO-able target' forgoes valuable tempo gusts (pulling a support/setup Pokemon to strand it)
hypotheses.pattern: prize-EV + real-damage (spread-aware) target selection promoted to shared perception

hypotheses.claim: Lillie's Determination fires on the generic hand<=5 gate and shuffles the hand into the deck while the player is holding an executable Phantom-Dive-enabling combo (e.g., Dragapult + Rare Candy + Fire), scattering the win condition.
hypotheses.direction: Lillie's should fire when hand is low-quality (no executable setup held), and be suppressed when the hand already contains an executable Dragapult-loading combo

threshold.value: Lillie's plays that shuffle away a held Dragapult+RareCandy/Fire combo <= 0.1

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: suppressing Lillie's too often keeps a clogged low-energy hand, missing the T1 8-card refuel
hypotheses.pattern: possession-based fire condition replacing generic hand-size threshold

hypotheses.claim: After a KO, L0 promotes the highest-displayed-damage Pokemon, promoting an unloaded (or Fire-less) Dragapult ex into the Active spot and exposing a 2-prize body it cannot swing with.
hypotheses.direction: post-KO promotion should choose a loaded attacker or a low-prize body, not an energy-less / Fire-less Dragapult ex
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: always promoting a cheap body can strand the real attacker on the bench behind a wall, reducing pressure
hypotheses.pattern: type-aware loaded check for promotion (Psychic-only Dragapult counts as unloaded)

hypotheses.claim: L0 plays stadiums unconditionally, so Risky Ruins is played (or kept) when it self-damages own low-HP basics on bench placement (verified -20 to every non-Dark basic benched: Budew 30->10, Dreepy 70->50), degrading own board more than the opponent's.
hypotheses.direction: Risky Ruins should be played only when own future bench placements are Dark/high-HP or Munkidori can export the self-damage; suppressed before Poffin-ing low-HP basics

threshold.value: RR-plays followed within 1 turn by self-benching a <=70HP non-Dark basic <= 0.2

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: never playing Risky Ruins forgoes opponent-basic chip and Munkidori fuel, and cedes the stadium slot to the opponent
hypotheses.pattern: board-state gate on stadium play (§2b RR condition)

hypotheses.claim: Munkidori Adrena-Brain (correctly Dark-gated by the engine, verified) still misfires on target/source selection: it moves counters to a full-HP tank (no KO) or off a Pokemon whose damage was needed, producing no board advancement.
hypotheses.direction: Adrena-Brain should fire only when the moved counters bring an opponent Pokemon into KO range or meaningfully advance a KO, sourcing from a Pokemon whose healing is also useful

threshold.value: share of Adrena-Brain uses that leave the target KO-able / KO'd >= 0.5

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: requiring an immediate KO forgoes the healing value of exporting self-damage off a Dragapult under pressure
hypotheses.pattern: real-damage/prize-EV target selection for counter-move ability

hypotheses.claim: Phantom Dive spread (6 free counters placed 'any way', verified 6->1 placement selects) is scattered one-per-bench-Pokemon instead of concentrated, so no single bench Pokemon reaches KO range for follow-up.
hypotheses.direction: the 6 counters should be concentrated onto 1-2 bench Pokemon that a follow-up (2nd Phantom Dive / Cruel Arrow / Boss's) can KO, unless a lethal is available elsewhere

threshold.value: median counters on the single most-loaded bench target >= 3 (of 6)

hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: always concentrating ignores spots where spreading finishes two separately-damaged targets
hypotheses.pattern: spread-placement heuristic keyed to follow-up KO plan

hypotheses.claim: Deckout: unconditional Ultra Ball (discard 2) plus heavy search thins the deck; but Lillie's shuffles the hand back and Night Stretcher recovers, so deckout horizon is ~14-16 turns and rarely reached.
hypotheses.direction: loss_share[deckout] should be low; if it rises, gate digging when deck is thin
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: stopping digging too early on a thick deck slows setup and reduces first_attack_turn quality
hypotheses.pattern: dig-stop when deck thin (mostly precautionary here)

hypotheses.claim: Rare Candy timing: if the engine never learns to Rare Candy Dreepy->Dragapult (offered, verified play option present 43x), it defaults to slow manual Drakloak evolution, delaying first_attack_turn(154) by ~1 turn.
hypotheses.direction: when Dreepy is in play (not this turn) and Dragapult is in hand, Rare Candy should be used to reach Phantom Dive a turn earlier
hypotheses.risk_of_overtightening: always Rare-Candying burns the 2 copies early and leaves nothing for a rebuild after the first Dragapult is KO'd
hypotheses.pattern: doctrine A/B (Rare Candy fast line vs manual evolution)
